$comment: B5 runtime vs incumbent (D-20260929-b5-runtime-ratchets): one downward-only ratchet per (package, incumbent) pair, ours ÷ theirs in-process. `ceiling` is what benchmarks/axes/runtime.ts gates each pair on; `target` is the bar every pair is held to in the end, at or below the incumbent. `history` is append-only and never rises: scripts/runtime-ratchets-lock.test.ts refuses a `ceiling` that is not the last entry, an entry above the one before it unless it cites a newer decision in .sdlc/decisions/, a history that rewrites the committed one, and a pair the axis measures with no ratchet (or a ratchet for no pair). A PR that makes a pair faster appends a lower step in the same commit; `npm run ratchets:propose` prints how far each can come down from the CI observations on main. Since D-20260930-b5-ceilings-from-spread each ceiling is max(mean + 3 sd, max) of the pair's CI series, written in its `derive.rule`; a pair with `bar` holds a spec's value and is never raised.

Gating at the bar rather than at 1.25x a measurement keeps R8 a requirement instead of a ratchet that starts above it.
